diff --git a/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh b/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh
new file mode 100755
index 00000000..09f85426
--- /dev/null
+++ b/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh
@@ -0,0 +1,1299 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# =============================================================================
+# ablation-grade.sh — the cycle-130 ablation grader (SDD §3.6, §5.7, D-4.7, D-4.8;
+# PRD FR-6 AC-6.1/6.2/6.4; DEC-0401, DEC-0413, DEC-0414, DEC-0420, DEC-0491, DEC-0493)
+#
+# Grades ONE run directory written by pipeline-run.sh against its task and writes
+# grade.json (the input ablation-row.sh joins into the runs.jsonl row), or
+# self-checks a task (--self-check) on a synthetic run built from the task itself.
+#
+# Usage:
+#   ablation-grade.sh <run-dir> <task-id> [--suite-root DIR] [--tasks-dir tasks|smoke]
+#                     [--out FILE] [--json] [--executor container|host]
+#                     [--image loa-ablation:258] [--docker-bin D]
+#                     [--allow-unfrozen] [--allow-partial]
+#   ablation-grade.sh --self-check base|reference|noisy --task-yaml F [--suite-root DIR]
+#                     [--executor …] [--image …] [--docker-bin D] [--json]
+#                     [--allow-unfrozen] [--allow-partial]
+#
+# Options:
+#   --suite-root DIR   suite root (default grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0; with
+#                      --self-check, the directory two levels above the task dir)
+#   --tasks-dir T      tasks (default) or smoke: the task is <root>/<T>/<task-id>/
+#   --out FILE         where grade.json goes (default <run-dir>/grade.json)
+#   --json             also print grade.json (self-check: the verdict object) on stdout
+#   --executor MODE    container (default; DEC-0491) or host
+#   --image IMG        the grading image (default loa-ablation:258)
+#   --docker-bin D     docker CLI (default $EVAL_DOCKER_BIN, else docker)
+#   --allow-unfrozen   grade although freeze.sh --check fails or the suite has no
+#                      MANIFEST.sha256 yet (task authoring only); grade.json records
+#                      suite_frozen: false. Without it a drift is exit 2 (DEC-0414).
+#   --allow-partial    passed to freeze.sh --check (fewer than four tasks per type)
+#   --self-check MODE  base | reference | noisy (noisy: review-catch only), see below
+#   --task-yaml F      the task to self-check (<root>/<tasks|smoke>/<id>/task.yaml)
+#
+# Reads ONLY (DEC-0413): <run-dir>/sandbox/, <run-dir>/snapshots/{index.json,<LABEL>.bundle},
+# <run-dir>/transcripts/events-*.jsonl, <run-dir>/eval/adversarial-{review,audit}.json,
+# the task's directory under the suite root (task.yaml, hidden/, fixture/), the suite's
+# MANIFEST.sha256 (through freeze.sh) and, for review-catch, the key manifest the task
+# names (review_catch.manifest) and its PR fixture (self-check only). It never reads
+# <run-dir>/meta/, the batch MANIFEST.json, or the sandbox copies of the dissent
+# envelopes (tamperable; the harness copies under eval/ are authoritative). It writes
+# only <run-dir>/grading/ and the --out file; nothing under sandbox/ is ever written.
+#
+# Freeze: freeze.sh --check --root <suite-root> runs first (with --smoke when the
+# suite manifest lists smoke/ paths, so a manifest frozen with --smoke checks as it
+# was frozen); a drift or a missing manifest refuses the grade (exit 2) unless
+# --allow-unfrozen.
+#
+# Grading trees (D-4.8) under <run-dir>/grading/<label>/, recreated on every call:
+#   final      sandbox/ as the agent left it, minus the top-level .git .claude CLAUDE.md
+#              .loa.config.yaml grimoires .run .beads .eval pr, every __pycache__ and
+#              .pytest_cache, and anything that is not a regular file, directory or
+#              symlink (a FIFO never blocks the copy)
+#   implement  the IMPLEMENT snapshot (snapshots/IMPLEMENT.bundle, commit
+#              index.json.implement): the tree REVIEW read; graded when REVIEW ran or
+#              when AUDIT ran without a fix1 snapshot
+#   fix1       the FIX1 snapshot: the tree AUDIT read; graded when AUDIT ran
+#   base       the task fixture: the baseline for regression_command (and, refactor,
+#              the suite-green-at-base check)
+# A snapshot is extracted with `git bundle unbundle` into a scratch bare repository and
+# `git archive <commit>` (a member that would land outside the tree is skipped). In
+# every tree each grader_protected path is restored from the fixture (a deleted file is
+# recreated, a modified one overwritten, a path the fixture lacks is removed; a
+# symlinked parent is replaced by a directory), then every hidden/manifest.json entry
+# is written at its dest (a same-named file is overwritten, a deleted directory
+# recreated). Churn (diff_lines, files_changed) compares the final tree against the
+# fixture before any restore: added + removed lines per changed text file (difflib),
+# every added, removed or modified file counted once; null for review-catch.
+#
+# Commands run INSIDE the image (DEC-0491):
+#   docker run --rm --network none --read-only --tmpfs /tmp:rw,size=256m --user <uid>:<gid>
+#     -v <tree>:/workspace:rw -w /workspace -e HOME=/tmp -e LC_ALL=C -e TMPDIR=/tmp
+#     <image> timeout 120 <cmd…>
+# `python3 -m pytest …` (or `pytest …`) becomes `python3 -I -s -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider
+# -q --rootdir /workspace -rA …` (one -q: -qq would drop the summary line; -rA lists every
+# outcome, from which the ids come); `bats …` becomes `bats --tap …` with BATS_LIB_PATH
+# unset (the -e set is the whole container environment). --executor host runs the same
+# argv in the tree under `env -i PATH HOME=<scratch> LC_ALL=C TMPDIR=<scratch>
+# PYTHONUSERBASE=<the caller's user base>` with pytest as `python3 -P -m pytest …`:
+# no -I or -s on the host, because the host's pytest lives in the user site (the Sprint
+# 258 smoke found no pytest under `-I -s`); PYTHONUSERBASE is passed for the same reason.
+#
+# Parsing: the pytest summary line (`N passed, M failed, K error …`) or TAP (`1..N`,
+# `ok`/`not ok`). A collection error is expanded to the test functions of its file; the
+# hidden total is never below the static case count of the hidden test files (`def test`
+# / `@test`). A command without a parseable summary counts total = that static count
+# (at least 1), passed = 0 when it exited non-zero (total when it exited 0), with
+# parse_error: true. Ids: "t<k>", k = the 1-based position of the case in file order
+# (pytest: path, then the line of its def; TAP: the test number); regression ids are
+# positions in the base run, newly_failing = failing at final, passing at base.
+#
+# Review-catch (DEC-0420): grading/gates-combined.md is the arm-neutral reduction: every
+# `path:line[-line]` citation (parser of recall-vs-defects.sh 1.1.2; the LOA-VERDICT
+# trailer removed first) from sandbox/review.md (the A0 contract),
+# sandbox/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/{engineer-feedback.md,auditor-sprint-feedback.md}
+# and each finding's anchor (and file:line) in eval/adversarial-{review,audit}.json,
+# one normalised `path:line[-line]` line each (pr/head/ → head/, a/ b/ and /workspace/
+# prefixes dropped), duplicates dropped. recall-vs-defects.sh <grading-dir> <pr-NN>
+# gates-combined.md (EVAL_MANIFEST_DIR = the manifest's directory) gives recall;
+# flags = its findings_cited; missed = defect positions ("d2"), never defect ids.
+# false_positives = citations within ±3 of no anchor, deduplicated by cited region
+# (same file, overlapping ±3 windows count once).
+#
+# Verdicts: the last `<!-- LOA-VERDICT {…} -->` trailer of engineer-feedback.md (review)
+# and auditor-sprint-feedback.md (audit); a gate ran when its feedback file exists.
+# verdict = {source_file, value}: the audit's, else the review's, else review.md's
+# `Verdict:` line (A0), else null. verdict_accuracy_per_gate {review, audit}: build —
+# true when APPROVED and the tree that gate read passes every hidden test, or
+# CHANGES_REQUIRED and it fails one; review-catch — true iff (CHANGES_REQUIRED) ==
+# (the key holds a high or critical defect); a gate without a trailer is false; a gate
+# that did not run is null. verdict_accuracy = audit's, else review's, else null.
+#
+# Contamination (D-4.7, DEC-0493): every tool_use input in transcripts/events-*.jsonl —
+# Bash command; Read/Grep/Glob file_path|path|pattern; Write/Edit/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit
+# file_path|notebook_path; WebFetch url; WebSearch query — is checked for: `hidden` (any
+# case) → hidden; grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0 → suite_path; 0xHoneyJar/loa →
+# repo_name; `git log … --all` or `git reflog` (Bash) → git_history; an absolute path

+def def_line(tree, path, func, cache):

+SYS_DIRS = ["/dev", "/proc", "/sys", "/usr", "/bin", "/sbin", "/lib", "/lib64", "/etc", "/opt", "/var"]
+GIT_HIST = re.compile(r"\bgit\b[^;&|\n]*\blog\b[^;&|\n]*--all\b|\bgit\b[^;&|\n]*\breflog\b")
+ABS_WORD = re.compile(r"(?:(?<=^)|(?<=[\s=:'\"`(<>|;&,]))(/[A-Za-z0-9._@+%=,:~-][A-Za-z0-9._@+%=,:~/-]*)")
+FIELDS = {"Bash": ["command"], "Read": ["file_path", "path"], "Grep": ["path", "pattern"], "Glob": ["path", "pattern"],
+          "Write": ["file_path"], "Edit": ["file_path"], "MultiEdit": ["file_path"], "NotebookEdit": ["notebook_path"],
+          "WebFetch": ["url"], "WebSearch": ["query"]}
+PATH_FIELDS = {"file_path", "path", "notebook_path"}

+def allowed_roots(run_dir, init_cwds):
+    if A.executor == "container":
+        return ["/workspace", "/tmp", "/home/evaluser"] + SYS_DIRS
+    home = os.path.expanduser("~")
+    sb = os.path.join(run_dir, "sandbox")
+    roots = {sb, os.path.realpath(sb), "/tmp"} | set(init_cwds)
+    roots |= {os.path.join(home, x) for x in (".claude", ".claude.json", ".codex", ".aws")}
+    return sorted(roots) + SYS_DIRS

+def outside(p, roots):
+    p = os.path.normpath(p)
+    return not any(p == r or p.startswith(r.rstrip("/") + "/") for r in roots)

+def check_value(tool, field, val, roots):
+    low = val.lower()
+    if "hidden" in low:
+        return "hidden"
+    if "grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0" in val:
+        return "suite_path"
+    if "0xhoneyjar/loa" in low:
+        return "repo_name"
+    if tool == "Bash" and GIT_HIST.search(val):
+        return "git_history"
+    cands = []
+    if field in PATH_FIELDS or (tool == "Glob" and field == "pattern"):
+        if val.startswith("/") and not val.startswith("//"):
+            cands.append(val)
+    elif tool == "Bash":
+        for w in ABS_WORD.findall(val):
+            if w.startswith("//") or re.match(r"^/[^/]+/$", w):
+                continue
+            cands.append(w)
+    for c in cands:
+        if outside(c, roots):

+    rank = lambda lbl: (PHASE_ORDER.index(lbl) if lbl in PHASE_ORDER else len(PHASE_ORDER), lbl)

+def tool_uses(ev):

+    for blk in content or []:

+def contamination(run_dir):
+    files = transcripts(run_dir)
+    events, cwds = [], set()

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------- git helpers
+def git(repo, *args, binary=False):
+    cmd = ["git", "-C", repo, "-c", "core.quotepath=off", "-c", "diff.noprefix=false", *args]
+    p = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, env=_git_env())
+    if p.returncode != 0:
+        raise RuntimeError(f"git {' '.join(args[:2])} failed: {p.stderr.decode('utf-8', 'replace').strip()}")
+    return p.stdout if binary else p.stdout.decode("utf-8", "replace")

+def _git_env():
+    env = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if k in ("PATH", "HOME", "LANG", "TMPDIR")}
+    env.update({"LC_ALL": "C", "GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM": "1", "GIT_PAGER": "cat", "GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF": ""})
+    return env

+def safe_path(p):
+    """A history path we are willing to write: relative, no `..`, printable, no backslash."""
+    return bool(p) and not p.startswith("/") and ".." not in p.split("/") and "\\" not in p \
+        and all(c.isprintable() for c in p)

+def mount_owned(p):
+    return any(part in MOUNT_OWNED for part in p.split("/"))

+def is_test(p):
+    parts = p.split("/")
+    base = parts[-1]
+    return "tests" in parts[:-1] or re.fullmatch(r"test_.*\.py|.*_test\.py", base) is not None or base.endswith(".bats")
+

+def runner_of(p):
+    if p.endswith(".bats"):
+        return "bats"
+    if p.endswith(".py") and re.fullmatch(r"test_.*\.py|.*_test\.py", p.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]):
+        return "pytest"
+    return None

+def under_roots(p, roots):
+    return any(p == r or p.startswith(r + "/") for r in roots)

+def commits_since(repo, since):
+    raw = git(repo, "log", f"--since={since}", "--no-merges", "--format=%H%x1f%P%x1f%cs%x1f%s%x1e")
+    for rec in raw.split("\x1e"):
+        rec = rec.strip("\n")
+        if not rec:
+            continue
+        sha, parents, date, subject = (rec.split("\x1f") + ["", "", ""])[:4]
+        yield sha, parents.split(), date, subject

+def changed_files(repo, parent, sha):
+    raw = git(repo, "diff", "--no-renames", "--name-status", "-z", parent, sha)
+    items = raw.split("\0")
+    files = []
+    i = 0
+    while i + 1 < len(items):
+        status, path = items[i], items[i + 1]
+        files.append((status[:1], path))
+        i += 2
+    return files

+def numstat(repo, parent, sha, paths=None):
+    args = ["diff", "--no-renames", "--numstat", parent, sha]
+    if paths:
+        args += ["--", *paths]
+    rows = []
+    for line in git(repo, *args).splitlines():
+        a, d, p = line.split("\t", 2)
+        rows.append((a, d, p))
+    return rows

+def blob(repo, commit, path):
+    """(mode, bytes) of path at commit, or None when absent."""
+    ls = git(repo, "ls-tree", "-z", commit, "--", path).split("\0")[0]
+    if not ls:
+        return None
+    meta, _ = ls.split("\t", 1)
+    mode, kind, obj = meta.split()
+    if kind != "blob":
+        return None
+    return mode, git(repo, "cat-file", "blob", obj, binary=True)

+def tree_files(repo, commit, prefix=None):
+    args = ["ls-tree", "-r", "-z", "--name-only", commit]
+    if prefix:
+        args += ["--", prefix]
+    return [p for p in git(repo, *args).split("\0") if p]

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------- materialise
+def write_file(root, rel, data):
+    if not safe_path(rel):
+        raise ValueError(f"unsafe path: {rel!r}")
+    dest = os.path.join(root, rel)
+    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(dest), exist_ok=True)
+    with open(dest, "wb") as fh:
+        fh.write(data)
+

+def put_from(repo, commit, rel, root, dest_rel=None):
+    b = blob(repo, commit, rel)
+    if b is None:
+        return False
+    mode, data = b
+    if mode == "120000":
+        raise ValueError(f"symlink in history: {rel}")
+    write_file(root, dest_rel or rel, data)
+    return True

+def helper_files(repo, commit, test_paths):
+    """Test infrastructure the tests rely on: conftest.py up to the root, helpers in each test dir, root runner configs."""
+    have = set(tree_files(repo, commit))
+    found = set()
+    for t in test_paths:
+        d = os.path.dirname(t)
+        parts = d.split("/") if d else []
+        for i in range(len(parts) + 1):
+            c = "/".join(parts[:i] + ["conftest.py"])
+            if c in have:
+                found.add(c)
+        for f in have:
+            if os.path.dirname(f) == d and f not in test_paths:
+                base = os.path.basename(f)
+                if base in ("conftest.py", "__init__.py") or base.endswith(".bash") or "helper" in base:
+                    found.add(f)
+    for f in INFRA_ROOT_FILES:
+        if f in have:
+            found.add(f)
+    return sorted(found)

+def sibling_files(repo, commit, sources, roots, exclude):
+    """The other non-test files in each touched source file's directory (the modules it most likely imports)."""
+    dirs = {os.path.dirname(p) for p in sources}
+    out = []
+    for f in tree_files(repo, commit):
+        if os.path.dirname(f) in dirs and f not in exclude and not is_test(f) and safe_path(f) \
+                and not mount_owned(f) and under_roots(f, roots):
+            out.append(f)
+    return sorted(out)

+def counts(output, runner):
+    if runner == "bats":
+        passed = len(re.findall(r"^ok ", output, re.M))
+        failed = len(re.findall(r"^not ok ", output, re.M))
+        return passed, failed
+    tail = output.strip().splitlines()[-1] if output.strip() else ""
+    num = lambda w: sum(int(n) for n in re.findall(r"(\d+) " + w, tail))
+    return num("passed"), num("failed") + num("errors?")

+def run_tests(tree, cmd, runner):
+    """Run the task's test command under env -i (plus the host's user base so a user-site pytest is found)."""
+    home = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="seed-home.")
+    env = {"PATH": os.environ.get("PATH", "/usr/bin:/bin"), "HOME": home, "LC_ALL": "C",
+           "PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE": "1", "PYTHONUSERBASE": site.getuserbase()}
+    argv = list(cmd)
+    if runner == "pytest":
+        argv = argv[:3] + ["-p", "no:cacheprovider"] + argv[3:]
+    elif runner == "bats" and os.environ.get("LOA_SEED_BATS"):
+        argv[0] = os.environ["LOA_SEED_BATS"]
+    try:
+        p = subprocess.run(argv, cwd=tree, env=env, capture_output=True, timeout=RUN_TIMEOUT)
+        text = (p.stdout + p.stderr).decode("utf-8", "replace")
+        rc = p.returncode
+    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
+        text, rc = "timeout", 124
+    except OSError as e:
+        text, rc = f"cannot run {argv[0]}: {e}", 127
+    finally:
+        shutil.rmtree(home, ignore_errors=True)
+    passed, failed = counts(text, runner)
+    return rc, passed, failed

+    if shutil.which("patch"):
+        cmd = ["patch", "-s", "-p1", "--no-backup-if-mismatch", "-i", patch_file]

+def subject_rest(subject):

+def sanitise(text, stems):

+    text = "".join(c if c.isprintable() else " " for c in text)
+    words = []

+                or re.match(r"[\W]*test_\w+", w) or "hidden" in w.lower() \
+                or any(s and s.lower() in w.lower() for s in stems):

+        else:

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------- selection
+def classify(mode, repo, sha, parents, roots):
+    """('candidate', files) | ('refused', path) | ('skipped', reason)."""
+    if len(parents) != 1:

+    for _, p in files:

+            return "skipped", f"outside the allowed roots: {p}"

+    sources = [p for _, p in files if not is_test(p)]

+        if not sources:
+            return "skipped", "no source file touched"

+        runners = {runner_of(p) for p in added_or_modified} - {None}
+        if not runners:
+            return "skipped", "no runnable test file (test_*.py, *_test.py, *.bats) added or changed"

+def covering_tests(repo, parent, sources, roots):

+    names = set()

+            if any(p.search(text) for p in pats):

+    ap.add_argument("--no-secrets", default="")
+    ap.add_argument("--since", required=True)
+    ap.add_argument("--select", type=int, default=4)
+    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True)
+    ap.add_argument("--repo")
+    ap.add_argument("--paths", default=DEFAULT_PATHS)
+    ap.add_argument("--suite-version", type=int, default=1)
+    ap.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")
+    try:
+        a = ap.parse_args(argv)
+    except SystemExit:
+        raise Usage("bad arguments (see --help)")
+    try:
+        datetime.date.fromisoformat(a.since)
+    except ValueError:
+        raise Usage(f"--since must be YYYY-MM-DD, got {a.since!r}")
+    if a.select < 1:
+        raise Usage("--select must be at least 1")
+    if a.suite_version < 1:
+        raise Usage("--suite-version must be at least 1")
+    a.repo = a.repo or a.repo_default
+    if subprocess.run(["git", "-C", a.repo, "rev-parse", "--git-dir"], capture_output=True).returncode != 0:
+        raise Usage(f"not a git repository: {a.repo}")
+    roots = [r.strip().strip("/") for r in a.paths.split(",") if r.strip().strip("/")]
+    if not roots or any(not safe_path(r) or mount_owned(r) for r in roots):
+        raise Usage(f"--paths must be relative roots outside the mount-owned paths: {a.paths!r}")
+    a.roots = roots
+    return a
+
+
+def main(argv):
+    global SUITE_VERSION
+    try:
+        a = parse(argv)
+    except Usage as e:
+        print(f"seed-{a_mode(argv)}: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
+        return 2
+    SUITE_VERSION = a.suite_version
+    name = f"seed-{a.mode}"
+    cands, refused, skipped = [], 0, 0
+    for sha, parents, date, subject in commits_since(a.repo, a.since):
+        if not SUBJECT[a.mode].match(subject):
+            continue
+        verdict, detail = classify(a.mode, a.repo, sha, parents, a.roots)
+        if verdict == "refused":
+            refused += 1
+            out(f"refused {sha[:12]}: {detail}")
+        elif verdict == "skipped":
+            skipped += 1
+            out(f"skipped {sha[:12]}: {detail}")
+        else:
+            cands.append((sha, parents[0], date, subject, detail))
+            out(f"candidate {sha[:12]} {date} {''.join(c if c.isprintable() else ' ' for c in subject)}")
+    selected = cands[: a.select]
+    if a.dry_run:
+        out(f"{name}: {len(cands)} candidate(s), {refused} refused, {skipped} skipped; dry run, nothing written")
+        return 0
+    tasks_dir = os.path.join(a.out, "tasks")
+    stage = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="seed-stage.")
+    written = failed = 0
+    taken = set()
+    try:
+        for sha, parent, date, subject, files in selected:
+            tid = next_id(tasks_dir, ID_PREFIX[a.mode], taken)
+            try:
+                if a.mode == "bugfix":
+                    tdir, info = build_bugfix(a.repo, sha, parent, date, subject, files, tid, stage, a.no_secrets, a.roots)
+                else:
+                    tdir, info = build_refactor(a.repo, sha, parent, date, subject, files, tid, stage, a.no_secrets, a.roots)
+            except (ValueError, RuntimeError, OSError) as e:
+                tdir, info = None, str(e)
+            if tdir == "secret":
+                refused += 1
+                out(f"refused {sha[:12]}: {info}")
+                taken.discard(tid)
+                continue
+            if tdir == "skip":
+                skipped += 1
+                out(f"skipped {sha[:12]}: {info}")
+                taken.discard(tid)
+                continue
+            if tdir is None:
+                failed += 1
+                out(f"proof-failed {sha[:12]}: {info}")
+                taken.discard(tid)
+                continue
+            os.makedirs(tasks_dir, exist_ok=True)
+            shutil.move(tdir, os.path.join(tasks_dir, tid))
+            written += 1
+            if a.mode == "bugfix":
+                out(f"proof {tid} {sha[:12]}: {info}")
+            else:
+                proof, churn = info.split("\t")
+                c = json.loads(churn)
+                out(f"proof {tid} {sha[:12]}: {proof}")
+                out(f"churn {tid}: files {c['files']}, insertions {c['insertions']}, deletions {c['deletions']}")
+                out(f"todo {tid}: author the structural check under hidden/structural/, list it in hidden/manifest.json "
+                    f"and set structural_check (validate-suite.sh requires it for refactor)")
+            out(f"wrote {os.path.join(tasks_dir, tid)}")
+    finally:
+        shutil.rmtree(stage, ignore_errors=True)
+    out(f"{name}: {len(cands)} candidate(s), {refused} refused, {skipped} skipped; "
+        f"selected {len(selected)}, written {written}, proof failed {failed}")
+    return 1 if failed else 0
+
+
+def a_mode(argv):
+    return argv[0] if argv and argv[0] in ("bugfix", "refactor") else "tasks"
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

+set -euo pipefail

+
+SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

+

+for a in "$@"; do [[ "$a" == "--help" || "$a" == "-h" ]] && usage 0; done
+[[ $# -gt 0 ]] || usage 2

+# PYTHONUSERBASE and PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 — and a clean

+    ap.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")

+        a = ap.parse_args(argv)
+    except SystemExit:

+    try:
+        datetime.date.fromisoformat(a.since)
+    except ValueError:
+        raise Usage(f"--since must be YYYY-MM-DD, got {a.since!r}")
+    if a.select < 1:
+        raise Usage("--select must be at least 1")
+    if a.suite_version < 1:
+        raise Usage("--suite-version must be at least 1")
+    a.repo = a.repo or a.repo_default

+        raise Usage(f"--paths must be relative roots outside the mount-owned paths: {a.paths!r}")
+    a.roots = roots
+    return a

+def main(argv):
+    global SUITE_VERSION
+    try:
+        a = parse(argv)
+    except Usage as e:
+        print(f"seed-{a_mode(argv)}: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
+        return 2
+    SUITE_VERSION = a.suite_version
+    name = f"seed-{a.mode}"
+    cands, refused, skipped = [], 0, 0
+    for sha, parents, date, subject in commits_since(a.repo, a.since):
+        if not SUBJECT[a.mode].match(subject):
+            continue
+        verdict, detail = classify(a.mode, a.repo, sha, parents, a.roots)
+        if verdict == "refused":
+            refused += 1
+            out(f"refused {sha[:12]}: {detail}")
+        elif verdict == "skipped":
+            skipped += 1
+            out(f"skipped {sha[:12]}: {detail}")
+        else:
+            cands.append((sha, parents[0], date, subject, detail))
+            out(f"candidate {sha[:12]} {date} {''.join(c if c.isprintable() else ' ' for c in subject)}")
+    selected = cands[: a.select]
+    if a.dry_run:
+        out(f"{name}: {len(cands)} candidate(s), {refused} refused, {skipped} skipped; dry run, nothing written")
+        return 0

+    stage = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="seed-stage.")

+    taken = set()

+            try:
+                if a.mode == "bugfix":

+                else:

+            if tdir == "secret":
+                refused += 1
+                out(f"refused {sha[:12]}: {info}")
+                taken.discard(tid)
+                continue
+            if tdir == "skip":
+                skipped += 1
+                out(f"skipped {sha[:12]}: {info}")
+                taken.discard(tid)
+                continue
+            if tdir is None:
+                failed += 1
+                out(f"proof-failed {sha[:12]}: {info}")
+                taken.discard(tid)
+                continue
+            os.makedirs(tasks_dir, exist_ok=True)
+            shutil.move(tdir, os.path.join(tasks_dir, tid))
+            written += 1
+            if a.mode == "bugfix":
+                out(f"proof {tid} {sha[:12]}: {info}")
+            else:
+                proof, churn = info.split("\t")
+                c = json.loads(churn)
+                out(f"proof {tid} {sha[:12]}: {proof}")
+                out(f"churn {tid}: files {c['files']}, insertions {c['insertions']}, deletions {c['deletions']}")
+                out(f"todo {tid}: author the structural check under hidden/structural/, list it in hidden/manifest.json "
+                    f"and set structural_check (validate-suite.sh requires it for refactor)")
+            out(f"wrote {os.path.join(tasks_dir, tid)}")
+    finally:
+        shutil.rmtree(stage, ignore_errors=True)
+    out(f"{name}: {len(cands)} candidate(s), {refused} refused, {skipped} skipped; "
+        f"selected {len(selected)}, written {written}, proof failed {failed}")
+    return 1 if failed else 0
+
+
+def a_mode(argv):
+    return argv[0] if argv and argv[0] in ("bugfix", "refactor") else "tasks"
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

+# eval/, meta/). docker is fixtures/docker-stub.sh through a wrapper that sets
+# DOCKER_STUB_PATH to $T/bin, where `python3` drops the image-only -I/-s flags (the
+# host's pytest lives in the user site) and `bats` is the operator's bats-core. The
+# tasks are built in a temporary suite root; the smoke self-checks run on a frozen copy
+# of grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0/smoke/.
+# =============================================================================

+  TESTS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
+  REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$TESTS_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
+  GRADER="$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh"
+  SMOKE="$REPO_ROOT/grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0/smoke"
+  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ag.XXXXXX")"

+  make_bf_py
+  make_bf_sh
+  make_rf_py
+  make_rc

+  chmod -R u+rwx "$T" 2>/dev/null || true
+  find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
+  rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true
+}
+
+make_bin() {
+  local ub
+  ub="$(python3 -c 'import site; print(site.getuserbase())')"

+#!/usr/bin/env bash

+#!/usr/bin/env bash

+# snap <run-dir> <LABEL>: commit and bundle the sandbox as pipeline-run.sh does after IMPLEMENT / FIX
+snap() {
+  local rd="$1" L="$2" c k
+  sg "$rd" add -A; sg "$rd" commit -q --allow-empty -m "snapshot $L"
+  c="$(sg "$rd" rev-parse HEAD)"; k="$(printf '%s' "$L" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z')"
+  sg "$rd" bundle create -q "$rd/snapshots/$L.bundle" HEAD
+  jq --arg k "$k" --arg c "$c" '.[$k] = $c' "$rd/snapshots/index.json" > "$rd/snapshots/i.tmp" && mv "$rd/snapshots/i.tmp" "$rd/snapshots/index.json"

+verdict() {

+apply_ref() { patch -s -p1 -d "$1/sandbox" < "$S/tasks/$(cat "$1.task")/hidden/reference.patch"; }
+# tool_use <run-dir> <LABEL> <tool> <input-json>: one assistant tool_use event line
+tool_use() {
+  jq -cn --arg t "$3" --argjson i "$4" '{type: "assistant", message: {content: [{type: "tool_use", name: $t, input: $i}]}}' \
+    >> "$1/transcripts/events-$2.jsonl"
+}
+grade() { run "$GRADER" "$@" --suite-root "$S" --allow-unfrozen --docker-bin "$T/docker"; }
+tree_digest() {
+  python3 -I -c '
+import hashlib, os, sys
+h = hashlib.sha256(); root = sys.argv[1]
+for r, ds, fs in os.walk(root):
+    ds.sort()
+    for n in sorted(ds + fs):
+        p = os.path.join(r, n); h.update(os.path.relpath(p, root).encode() + b"\0")
+        if os.path.islink(p): h.update(b"L" + os.readlink(p).encode())
+        elif os.path.isfile(p): h.update(open(p, "rb").read())
+print(h.hexdigest())' "$1"
+}

+sg() { local rd="$1"; shift; git -C "$rd/sandbox" -c user.email=e@l -c user.name=eval -c commit.gpgsign=false "$@"; }

+# make_run <task-id> <run-dir>: the task fixture (or the PR under pr/) committed as base
+make_run() {
+  local id="$1" rd="$2" td="$S/tasks/$1"
+  mkdir -p "$rd/sandbox" "$rd/snapshots" "$rd/transcripts" "$rd/eval" "$rd/meta"
+  echo "$id" > "$rd.task"   # beside the run dir, for apply_ref
+  if [[ -d "$td/fixture" ]]; then cp -a "$td/fixture/." "$rd/sandbox/"
+  else mkdir -p "$rd/sandbox/pr"; cp -a "$T/prs/pr-77/." "$rd/sandbox/pr/"; fi
+  sg "$rd" init -q
+  printf '%s\n' '/.claude/' '/CLAUDE.md' '/.loa.config.yaml' '/grimoires/' '/.run/' '/.beads/' '/.eval/' >> "$rd/sandbox/.git/info/exclude"
+  sg "$rd" add -A; sg "$rd" commit -q --allow-empty -m base
+  jq -n --arg b "$(sg "$rd" rev-parse HEAD)" '{base: $b}' > "$rd/snapshots/index.json"
+  mkdir -p "$rd/sandbox/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1" "$rd/sandbox/.claude"
+  echo "# mount" > "$rd/sandbox/CLAUDE.md"
+  printf '{"run_id": "r-%s", "status": "completed", "arm": "a1_full"}\n' "$id" > "$rd/meta/pipeline.json"
+  echo a1_full > "$rd/meta/arm"
+}
+# snap <run-dir> <LABEL>: commit and bundle the sandbox as pipeline-run.sh does after IMPLEMENT / FIX
+snap() {
+  local rd="$1" L="$2" c k
+  sg "$rd" add -A; sg "$rd" commit -q --allow-empty -m "snapshot $L"
+  c="$(sg "$rd" rev-parse HEAD)"; k="$(printf '%s' "$L" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z')"
+  sg "$rd" bundle create -q "$rd/snapshots/$L.bundle" HEAD
+  jq --arg k "$k" --arg c "$c" '.[$k] = $c' "$rd/snapshots/index.json" > "$rd/snapshots/i.tmp" && mv "$rd/snapshots/i.tmp" "$rd/snapshots/index.json"
+}
+# verdict <run-dir> review|audit <VERDICT> [body]
+verdict() {
+  local f=engineer-feedback.md; [[ "$2" == audit ]] && f=auditor-sprint-feedback.md
+  printf '# Feedback\n\n%s\n\n<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"%s","verdict":"%s","counts":{"critical":0,"high":1}} -->\n' "${4:-}" "$2" "$3" \
+    > "$1/sandbox/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/$f"
+}
+apply_ref() { patch -s -p1 -d "$1/sandbox" < "$S/tasks/$(cat "$1.task")/hidden/reference.patch"; }
+# tool_use <run-dir> <LABEL> <tool> <input-json>: one assistant tool_use event line
+tool_use() {
+  jq -cn --arg t "$3" --argjson i "$4" '{type: "assistant", message: {content: [{type: "tool_use", name: $t, input: $i}]}}' \
+    >> "$1/transcripts/events-$2.jsonl"
+}
+grade() { run "$GRADER" "$@" --suite-root "$S" --allow-unfrozen --docker-bin "$T/docker"; }
+tree_digest() {
+  python3 -I -c '
+import hashlib, os, sys
+h = hashlib.sha256(); root = sys.argv[1]
+for r, ds, fs in os.walk(root):
+    ds.sort()
+    for n in sorted(ds + fs):
+        p = os.path.join(r, n); h.update(os.path.relpath(p, root).encode() + b"\0")
+        if os.path.islink(p): h.update(b"L" + os.readlink(p).encode())
+        elif os.path.isfile(p): h.update(open(p, "rb").read())
+print(h.hexdigest())' "$1"
+}

+#!/usr/bin/env bash

+    run "$H/pipeline-run.sh" --task-yaml "$S/tasks/bf-py/task.yaml" --arm a1_full --run-dir "$T/e2e" --run-id r-e2e \

+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]

+  [ "$(G '.verdicts | "\(.review) \(.audit)"')" = "CHANGES_REQUIRED APPROVED" ]

+  [ "$(jq -r '"\(.hidden_test_pass_rate * 7 | round) \(.verdict_accuracy_review) \(.verdict_accuracy_audit) \(.regressions)"' <<<"$output")" = "5 true false 0" ]

+# --- review-catch (DEC-0420) -----------------------------------------------------------------
+
+@test "AG-8 gates-combined.md reduces review.md, both feedback files and both eval/ envelopes; recall and deduplicated false positives" {
+  RD="$T/run"; make_run rc-x "$RD"
+  A="$RD/sandbox/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1"
+  printf 'head/lib/x.sh:5 — the guard is gone\nVerdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED\n' > "$RD/sandbox/review.md"
+  verdict "$RD" review APPROVED 'lib/x.sh:12 reads a stale value'
+  verdict "$RD" audit CHANGES_REQUIRED 'pr/head/lib/x.sh:13 the same stale value'
+  echo '{"findings": [{"anchor": "lib/x.sh:20", "severity": "low"}]}' > "$RD/eval/adversarial-review.json"
+  echo '{"findings": [{"file": "lib/x.sh", "line": 28, "severity": "medium"}]}' > "$RD/eval/adversarial-audit.json"
+  # the sandbox copy of an envelope is tamperable and never read
+  echo '{"findings": [{"anchor": "lib/x.sh:2"}]}' > "$A/adversarial-review.json"
+  grade "$RD" rc-x
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  [ "$(cat "$RD/grading/gates-combined.md" | tr '\n' ' ')" = "head/lib/x.sh:5 lib/x.sh:12 head/lib/x.sh:13 lib/x.sh:20 lib/x.sh:28 " ]
+  [ "$(G '.recall | "\(.defects_seeded) \(.defects_caught) \(.recall == 1) \(.flags) \(.missed | length)"')" = "2 2 true 5 0" ]
+  [ "$(G '.false_positives')" = 2 ]      # 12 and 13 share a ±3 region; 28 is another
+  [ "$(G '.hidden_tests')" = null ] && [ "$(G '.diff_lines')" = null ]
+  # the key holds a high defect: CHANGES_REQUIRED is accurate, APPROVED is not
+  [ "$(G '.verdict_accuracy_per_gate | "\(.review),\(.audit)"')" = "false,true" ]
+  [ "$(G '.verdict_accuracy')" = true ]
+  # without the envelopes the low defect is missed, by position only
+  rm "$RD/eval/adversarial-review.json"
+  grade "$RD" rc-x
+  [ "$(G '.recall | "\(.defects_caught) \(.missed | join(","))"')" = "1 d2" ]
+}

+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+# =============================================================================
+# evals/tests/seed-refactor.bats — cycle-130 Sprint 259 Task 2.3 (SDD §5.14,

+#
+# seed-refactor-tasks.sh over a throwaway git repo: a refactor commit touching
+# two source files with the tests unchanged and green becomes a task with the
+# churn recorded (task.yaml source.churn and the printed churn line, equal to
+# git diff --numstat), the suite green at both ends, the structural check left

+# --dry-run writes nothing; a refactor that breaks the suite fails its proof.

+setup() {
+  TESTS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"

+  export LOA_EVAL_PHASE_PROMPTS_DIR="$T/no-prompts"
+  python3 -m pytest --version >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "pytest not importable by python3"
+  git init -q -b main "$G"
+  mkdir -p "$G/tools/fmt/tests"
+  cat > "$G/tools/fmt/left.py" <<'PY'
+def left(s, width):
+    s = str(s)
+    if len(s) >= width:
+        return s
+    return s + " " * (width - len(s))
+PY
+  cat > "$G/tools/fmt/right.py" <<'PY'
+def right(s, width):
+    s = str(s)
+    if len(s) >= width:
+        return s
+    return " " * (width - len(s)) + s
+PY
+  cat > "$G/tools/fmt/tests/conftest.py" <<'PY'
+import os, sys
+sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), ".."))
+PY
+  cat > "$G/tools/fmt/tests/test_fmt.py" <<'PY'
+from left import left
+from right import right
+
+def test_left():
+    assert left("ab", 4) == "ab  "
+    assert left("abcde", 4) == "abcde"
+
+def test_right():
+    assert right(7, 3) == "  7"
+PY
+  gc add -A; gc commit -q -m "chore: initial"
+}

+    return " " * max(0, width - len(str(s)))
+PY
+  printf 'from pad import gap\n\n\ndef left(s, width):\n    return str(s) + gap(s, width)\n' > "$G/tools/fmt/left.py"
+  printf 'from pad import gap\n\n\ndef right(s, width):\n    return gap(s, width) + str(s)\n' > "$G/tools/fmt/right.py"

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# evals/tests/validate-suite.bats — cycle-130 Sprint 258 Task 1.11 (DEC-0424,

#

setup() {
  TESTS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
  REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$TESTS_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

}

teardown() {
  find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true

# (fixtures/ablation/suite-lib.bash): each check's pass and fail — schema, the
# four-by-four counts (relaxed by --allow-partial), the test_command allowlist,
# hidden/manifest.json destinations, the fixture path rule, leakage strings in
# TASK.md / criterion / phase prompts, the suite file's task_types.
# =============================================================================

setup() {
  TESTS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
  REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$TESTS_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
  VS="$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/validate-suite.sh"
  SUITE="$REPO_ROOT/evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml"
  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/vs.XXXXXX")"
  R="$T/suite"; mkdir -p "$R"
  # no phase prompts unless a test supplies them
  export LOA_EVAL_PHASE_PROMPTS_DIR="$T/no-prompts"
  # shellcheck source=fixtures/ablation/suite-lib.bash
  source "$TESTS_DIR/fixtures/ablation/suite-lib.bash"
}

teardown() {
  find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
  rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true
}

cat > /workspace/review.md <<'EOF'
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:714 — `tf.extractall(tree, filter=keep)` (and `tarfile.data_filter` on line 710) only exist on Python 3.12+ / 3.11.4+ / 3.10.12+. On a stock Debian 12 host (python3 3.11.2) every build-task grade that has an IMPLEMENT/FIX1 bundle dies with `internal error: TypeError: TarFile.extractall() got an unexpected keyword argument 'filter'` (exit 2, no grade.json) — reproduced here; nothing in the script declares or checks a minimum Python. Guard the filter (fall back to a manual member loop that applies the same safe_rel/EXCLUDE checks) or require Python ≥ 3.12 explicitly in the header and a startup check.
head/evals/tests/ablation-grade.bats:16 — `BATS_BIN="$HOME/.local/dotfiles/tools/diff-so-fancy/test/bats/bin/bats"` is a hard-coded path from one developer's machine; `ln -s "$BATS_BIN" "$T/bin/bats"` then gives a dangling symlink everywhere else, so AG-2 (bf-sh), AG-7 and the bats-shaped smoke self-checks fail for anyone but the author. Use the repo convention (`LOA_EVAL_BATS_BIN`, else `command -v bats`) as pipeline-run.bats / fingerprint.sh do.
head/evals/harness/lib/seed_tasks.py:570 — `selected = cands[: a.select]` fixes the N selected candidates before build_bugfix/build_refactor run, so a build-stage "skip" (refactor: no covering test at the parent) or a no-secrets "refused" consumes one of the --select slots and fewer tasks than requested are written even when later candidates qualify. This contradicts both wrapper headers (seed-bugfix-tasks.sh:40 "refusals and skips do not count", seed-refactor-tasks.sh:38 "a commit without a covering test is skipped and does not count"). Iterate over cands until `written + failed == select` instead of slicing up front.
head/evals/harness/lib/seed_tasks.py:229 — the `patch`-less fallback `git apply -p1 <file>` run with cwd=<proof tree> is unsafe when the temporary proof tree happens to lie inside a git work tree (e.g. TMPDIR under a checkout, as in this sandbox): git apply resolves paths against that repository, prints "Skipped patch" and exits 0, so apply_patch() returns True with the fixture unchanged. For refactor the proof is then vacuous (green at base and "green at reference" without the patch) and a task is written whose reference.patch was never proven; for bugfix it surfaces as a misleading "not red at base/not green at reference". Verified here. Run the fallback with a guard that forces non-repository mode (e.g. `GIT_DIR=/dev/null` is not enough — use `git apply --unsafe-paths --directory` from a confirmed non-repo cwd, or require `patch` and fail loudly) and check the patch actually changed the tree.

Write null for `value` (keeping source_file) or document "none" in the grade.json contract.
Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED
EOF

content.text:
Review written to `review.md`. Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED. Nothing under `pr/` was modified.

**What I checked.** I read the full diff (grader, seeder library and wrappers, corpus seeder change, validator change, six test files, fixture manifests). The two rewritten manifests match their new SHA256SUMS, and the only rows removed are generated-artefact fix regions, with defect labels untouched. The embedded Python compiles, and I exercised the grader's parsing, citation, false-positive, churn and contamination helpers directly. I ran the two new seeder test files against a scratch copy with stubs for the missing no-secrets grader and suite file, and graded synthetic bug-fix and refactor runs end to end in host mode.

**Findings, most serious first:**

- **Grader crashes on common Pythons.** The snapshot extractor uses the `filter=` keyword of `TarFile.extractall`, which exists only from Python 3.11.4 or 3.12. On this box's 3.11.2 every build grade with an IMPLEMENT or FIX1 bundle exits 2 with an internal error and writes no grade. Reproduced.
- **Test file depends on one developer's machine.** The new bats file hard-codes a bats binary under a personal dotfiles path. On any other host the symlink dangles and the bats-shaped tests fail. The repo already has a convention via an environment variable.
- **Seeder selection contradicts its documentation.** Candidates are sliced to N before building, so a refactor skipped for lacking covering tests, or a secret refusal, consumes a slot. Both wrapper headers promise the opposite.
- **Patch fallback can pass a vacuous proof.** Without `patch`, the seeder falls back to `git apply` in the proof tree. When that tree lies inside a git work tree, git skips the paths and exits 0, so a refactor's proof is green at both ends without the patch ever applying. Reproduced here because this sandbox's TMPDIR is inside the checkout.
- **Undocumented verdict value.** A gate file without a trailer yields the string "none" in the grade's verdict value, which the header does not list.

**What passed.** With TMPDIR outside any repo, nine of ten seeder tests pass. The tenth fails only because this box has no `patch`. After working around the tarfile call on my scratch copy, the grader produced correct hidden, regression, snapshot, verdict-accuracy, churn and contamination values, restored tampered protected files, and skipped a FIFO cleanly. The corpus-seeder and validator changes look correct.

**Not verifiable here.** Container mode, the freeze and recall scripts, the smoke tasks and the pipeline end-to-end test depend on repository files outside this PR.
